chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Recording with Tatum: 'Battery Bounce' and bad timing
summary: Collins recorded with Tatum only once or twice, on unamplified guitar before the army, and missed a second chance when he left for Nat.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I recorded with -- it's a funny thing. I only recorded with Art once. No, I didn't. Once or twice. It just so happened in Chicago during that time we weren't doing any recording when I started with him at the Duces. When I went to New York, this is when I recorded with him. But I left and went to the army, you know.
It was right before you went into the army.
Yeah, that's right. And as I told you, I
did this recording with him, with an unamplified guitar. Now, I'm sure the name of the tune was -- that I had a solo on was Battery Bounce.

Now, it's a funny thing. As much as I worked with him, now I went -- I started working with him again and we were getting ready to record and I joined Nat. And this is just -- timing is everything, isn't it?
You know. So that was why --
